key_insight: PolyGPT generates highly valid polymer structures, but electrolyte conditioning increases repetition and reduces the yield satisfying combined design requests.
engineering_relevance: Polymer electrolyte screening should prioritize distinct, valid, target-matching candidates absent from the training catalog rather than property error alone.
method: Use a 38.3-million-parameter decoder-only Transformer to generate polymer repeat units.
Condition generation on optional property targets, chemical-feature inclusion or exclusion, and electrolyte domain.
Compare conditioning strategies and nine checkpoints using validity, uniqueness, catalog novelty, and request satisfaction.
evidence_signal: At a Tg target of 246.11 K, electrolyte conditioning slightly improved predictor-estimated error from 26.97 to 26.07 K, but reduced the fraction of attempts yielding distinct, valid, catalog-unseen polymers within 50 K from 59.90% to 19.71%.
watch_item: Predictor-estimated Tg agreement does not establish experimental performance, and validation-loss checkpoint selection may not maximize useful candidate yield.
paper_title: PolyGPT: A Decoder-Only Transformer for Polymer Electrolyte Design
